android_mechanism: List rows are re-created during scrolling instead of being recycled
bug_description: The browsing-history dialog renders each day's entries with a plain ForEach inside ListItemGroup, so when the dialog opens, HistoryItem components for every recorded entry (including off-screen ones) are created eagerly, and scrolling re-creates components instead of recycling them. Opening the history dialog and scrolling it is slow once history grows.
fix_summary: History entries are rendered with LazyForEach backed by a per-group IDataSource implementation, so row components are created on demand as they enter the viewport and recycled while scrolling.

test_oracle.definition: raw-instruction-retired sample count attributed to the app process during the measured step, aggregated from perf.data (HapRay perf.db instruction counts).
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed over >= 3 rounds per variant

evidence.note: 9.64G vs 2.79G instructions (3.5x); cpu 5986 vs 4041 ms; builds 200 vs 59

mechanism_oracle.definition: (a) Time from dialog-open event to first rendered history frame; (b) count of HistoryItem component build/attach operations in the ace trace during the whole scroll; (c) dropped-frame count while scrolling.
mechanism_oracle.comparison: unfixed builds all N components at open (N = seeded entries) vs fixed builds only visible rows (~10-15); unfixed_first_frame_ms > fixed_first_frame_ms; unfixed shows more jank frames during scroll.

reproduction: git -C hosts/browser checkout case/browser_history_list_foreach/unfixed; apply the measurement harness patch for this case, build, sign and install the HAP.
git -C hosts/browser checkout case/browser_history_list_foreach/fixed; rebuild, reinstall and repeat identically.
Compare test_oracle.metric across the two report sets: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed.
